transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what brought me in is I kind of got… really wrapped up in this park idea. I’m usually just a regular crew guy, landscaping, you know, but I started trying to handle like three bids at once, calling city people, lining up plant suppliers, messaging everybody I knew about it.

At first it felt productive, like I was just being motivated, but it got to where I couldn’t really shut it off. I don’t know if that makes sense, but it felt like maybe it was getting to be too much.
Have you noticed any time recently where your mood was unusually high, elated, or irritable, where you felt like you were on top of the world or really agitated?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say “on top of the world” exactly, but before I kind of crashed, I did feel really fired up. Like bigger than myself, I guess. It felt like I could make the whole thing happen if people would just get on board.

And… I’m not proud of this, but if a coworker questioned the plan or told me to slow down, I’d snap at him way harder than made sense. I knew afterward it was too much, but in the moment it felt like they were getting in the way.
Was there a specific period of time — at least a few days or more — where you felt this way most of the day, nearly every day, not just in short bursts?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it wasn’t just like an hour here or there. It kind of started when I was trying to, I don’t know, remake myself for that park pitch—like really prove I could handle it.

I’d say it lasted maybe about two weeks before I sort of… crashed. Most days during that stretch I was pretty fired up about it. I didn’t really see it as a problem at first, though. It felt more like I was just being focused, if that makes sense.
Was there a time when your mood was so high or your energy so intense that other people could notice a clear change in you — like you weren’t acting like your usual self at all?

Yeah… I think people noticed. I mean, I didn’t think I was acting that different at the time — I thought I was just really motivated, you know?

But before I crashed, I was pretty fired up, almost like… bigger than myself, I guess. And if someone at work questioned the plan or told me to slow down, I’d snap at them way harder than made sense. Not like me, really. I know that doesn’t sound great.
Can you describe what it was like when you 'crashed' after those two weeks? Did your mood drop significantly or did you feel unusually low, or was it more just feeling tired or burnt out?

It wasn’t just tired, I don’t think. I mean, I wish it was just burnout, because that sounds more normal.

My mood dropped pretty hard after that. And honestly… it’s kind of been hanging over me for about a year now, just this low thing that doesn’t really lift. But this latest crash after those two weeks was probably the worst it’s gotten.

Does that answer what you mean?
After you 'crashed,' did you experience a period of at least two weeks where you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually care about?

Yeah… I think it was definitely more than two weeks. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but that low feeling has kind of been hanging around for about a year, honestly.

After that crash, though, it got worse than usual. Like, the heaviest it’s been. I kept hoping it would just pass and I’d get back to normal, but it didn’t really lift. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
After you crashed and the low feeling got worse than usual, did you lose interest in things you normally enjoy, feel hopeless, or have trouble doing things you used to do easily?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I guess I have lost interest in stuff.

Like, I used to go hiking to clear my head, and I’d take pictures of creek beds or trees or whatever if the light looked good. Lately I’ll still maybe go out there, but I just leave the camera in the truck. Even if it’s a perfect shot, I just… don’t really care enough to grab it.

I don’t know if that counts, but it’s definitely not how I usually am.

During that time when you felt really fired up and bigger than yourself, did you ever feel so hyper or out of control that someone close to you suggested you needed help or thought you were acting dangerously different?

I don’t know if anyone said I needed help exactly… not in those words. But yeah, before I crashed, I was really fired up, like I felt bigger than myself almost.

And at work, if a coworker questioned my plan or told me to slow down, I’d snap at him way harder than made sense. I’d tell myself I was just being decisive or trying to get things done, but looking back, it probably came off pretty different. Does that count as what you’re asking?
Since the crash, have you had days where you felt so down that you couldn’t get out of bed, had trouble concentrating, or even thought about hurting yourself?

Um… yeah. I mean, I don’t want you to think I’m, like, trying to be dramatic or anything, but it did get scary.

There was one day after work I was sitting in my truck, and it wasn’t just that normal “I wish I could disappear” kind of thought. I caught myself thinking about exactly how I could end it with what I had there in the truck, and that scared me pretty bad.

I haven’t really wanted to say that out loud, but… yeah, that happened.
